To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nitric oxide (a gaseous messenger molecule) and cGIMP (a cyclic nucleotide) are involved in the regulation of the blood-brain-barrier.
the endothelium and the astrocyte of the brain capillary form NO and cAMP in response to different physiological stimuli.
NO/cGMP signaling is a relevant mechanism of signal transduction in both BCEC and AC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the role of NO/cGMP in the regulation of BBB properties.
the role of NO and cGIMP in the BBB.
the role of NO and cGAMP for the function of the BBB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NO is not the only mediator of endothelium-derived relaxation and that NO/cGMP is not the only signal transduction pathway involved in the regulation of endothelial cell function and the BBB.
NO/cGMP is involved in the regulation of BCEC and AC function, which is important for the integrity of the BBB.
NO/cGMP is not only a mediator of vasodilation, but also an important factor in signal transduction of BCEC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NO is an important mediator for the function of BCEC and AC and that NO/cGMP/PKG/VASP signaling pathways are involved in the regulation of BBB function.
NO/cGMP is a signal transduction pathway in BCEC and astrocytes, which can be activated in a variety of ways and which is associated with the function of the BBB.
the NO-cGMP-PKG-VASP pathway is a possible target for the regulation of the BBB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NO/cGMP is a relevant signaling system in brain capillary EC and astrocytes, which is important for the formation of the blood-brain-barrier.
the endothelium of the blood-brain-barrier (BBB) is capable of forming NO and cGmp in response to different signals.
NO/cGMP signaling is involved in the function of BCEC and that this signaling pathway may be relevant for the regulation of the BBB.
